heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF PASANGKAYU REGENCY
translated_text:
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PASANGKAYU REGENCY

NUMBER 9 OF 2019

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE REGENT OF PASANGKAYU,

Considering:

a. that women and children are creations of Almighty God who constitute important elements of Indonesian society and Nation;
b. that in social life women and children often experience violence or unpleasant treatment;
c. that all forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination;
d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children.

In View of:

1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia;
2. Law Number 7 of 2003 concerning the Establishment of East Luwu Regency and North Mamuju Regency in South Sulawesi Province (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2003 Number 27, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4270;
3. Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014 Number 244, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5587) as last amended by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2015 Number 58, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5679;

With Mutual Approval of

THE REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES OF PASANGKAYU REGENCY

and

THE REGENT OF PASANGKAYU

HAS DECIDED:

To Establish:

REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN.

heading: CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Pasangkayu Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Pasangkayu.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person who is recognized by law as a Woman.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child in the womb.
7. Protection is all service actions to fulfill rights, as well as guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence.
8. Protection of Women is an effort aimed at protecting Women and their rights in order to obtain a sense of security from acts of violence.
9. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
11. Victim of violence hereinafter referred to as victim is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.
14. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

heading: CHAPTER II
translated_text:
CHAPTER II

OBJECTIVES AND SCOPE

Article 2

The objectives of protection of Women and Children are to:
a. provide and enhance a sense of security for Women and Children;
b. help prevent acts of Violence against Women and Children;
c. help prevent exploitation activities against Women and Children.
d. provide Services to Women and Children in facing legal problems; and
e. help improve the quality of life of Women and Children.

heading: Article 3
CHAPTER III
JDIH PASANGKAYU REGENCY
translated_text:
JDIH PASANGKAYU REGENCY

Article 5

Physical violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

heading: Article 6
translated_text:
Article 6

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 4 letter b is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

heading: Article 7
translated_text:
Article 7

Sexual violence as referred to in Article 4 letter c is in the form of:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse; and/or
c. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

heading: Article 8
JDIH PASANGKAYU REGENCY
translated_text:
JDIH PASANGKAYU REGENCY

Article 9

Exploitation as referred to in Article 4 letter e is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the Victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or Services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the Victim to obtain benefits not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

DUTIES AND AUTHORITIES

Part One

Duties

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

Duties of Regional Government in the Protection of Women

heading: Article 12
translated_text:
Article 12

1. The Regional Government is obliged to carry out the Protection of Women in the Region.
2. Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by preparing a strategic plan for the Protection of Women for the long term, medium term, and short term.
3. The strategic preparation as referred to in paragraph (2) must be integrated with the Regional development planning documents.
4. The Regional Government in preparing the strategic plan as referred to in paragraph (3) may involve the community, social institutions and/or other institutions that carry out activities related to the Protection of Women.

heading: Article 13
translated_text:
Article 13

1. The Regional Government is obliged to prevent acts of Violence against Women.
2. Prevention of acts of Violence against Women as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in the form of activities:
a. Regional Action Plan;
c. preparation of an effective information system; and
d. cooperation with institutions that have activities in preventing acts of Violence against Women.

heading: Article 14
translated_text:
Article 14

The Regional Government is obliged to assist in handling acts of Violence against Women.

heading: Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Duties of Regional Government in the Protection of Children

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

1. The Regional Government is obliged to carry out the Protection of Children in the Region.
2. Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by preparing a strategic plan for the Protection of Children for the long term, medium term, and short term.
3. The strategic preparation as referred to in paragraph (2) must be integrated with the Regional development planning documents.
4. The Regional Government in preparing the strategic plan as referred to in paragraph (3) may involve the community, social institutions and/or other institutions that carry out activities related to the Protection of Children.

heading: Article 16
translated_text:
Article 16

The Regional Government provides guidance and direction for Children to embrace religion in accordance with the religion and beliefs of their parents.

heading: Article 17
translated_text:
Article 17

1. The Regional Government is obliged to provide comprehensive health facilities for Children.
2. Comprehensive health facilities as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of community health centers and hospitals.
3. Comprehensive health as referred to in paragraph (1) includes promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts, both for basic health Services and referrals.
4. Comprehensive health as referred to in paragraph (3) is provided free of charge for families who are unable or poor families.
5. The Regional Government carries out activities to support the provision of breast milk to infants.

heading: Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

1. The Regional Government is obliged to provide primary and secondary education for Children.
2. In providing education as referred to in paragraph (1) the Regional Government provides education cost assistance or free education for students who come from poor families and/or neglected Children.

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

1. The Regional Government is obliged to accommodate and/or care for Children who are neglected by their parents and/or family.
2. Accommodation and/or care of Children as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out through cooperation with institutions, social foundations, or Orphanages.

heading: JDIH KABUPATEN PASANGKAYU
translated_text:
JDIH KABUPATEN PASANGKAYU

Article 20

1. The Regional Government is obliged to provide special Protection for Children who are Victims of unrest or Victims of natural disasters.
2.  Special protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of fulfillment of:
a. basic needs consisting of food, clothing, housing, education, health, learning and recreation, security guarantees, and equal treatment; and
b. special needs for Children with disabilities and Children who experience psychosocial disorders.

heading: Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

1. The Regional Government is obliged to prevent efforts and acts of violence against Children.
2. Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in the form of activities that include:
a. early detection and intervention;
b. socialization, seminars or workshops;
c. preparation of an effective information system; and
d. cooperation with institutions that have activities in preventing acts of violence against Children.

heading: Article 22
translated_text:
Article 22

The Regional Government is obliged to assist in handling acts of Violence against Children.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Authorities

heading: Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

1. The Regional Government has the authority to:
a. accommodate Victims of acts of Violence against Women and Children; and
b. accommodate and/or care for neglected Children.
2. The Regional Government in exercising the authority as referred to in paragraph (1) may cooperate with related parties.

heading: JDIH KABUPATEN PASANGKAYU
translated_text:
JDIH KABUPATEN PASANGKAYU

Article 24

1. Related parties as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) are:
a. social community organizations, institutions or orphanages that have activities related to the protection, care, accommodation, guidance, empowerment of Children and/or Women;
b. social workers or volunteers;
c. advocates; and
d. religious leaders.
2. Cooperation as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) is carried out in the form of a cooperation agreement.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

HANDLING OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 25

1. The Regional Government shall prepare medical personnel at community health centers or at hospitals specifically handling Victims of Violence against Women and Children.
2. Medical personnel as referred to in paragraph (1) shall provide complete health services to Victims of Violence against Women and Children.

heading: Article 26
heading_path: HANDLING OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 26

1. The Regional Government shall assist in providing special rooms for Victims of Violence against Women and Children.
2. Special rooms as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be located at the Resort Police and at every Sector Police in the Region.

heading: Article 27
heading_path: HANDLING OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 27

1. Social workers or volunteer personnel as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (1) letter b shall have the duty to accompany Victims in facing the process of resolving acts of violence.
2. In carrying out duties as referred to in paragraph (1), social workers or volunteer personnel shall conduct activities:
a. counseling or guidance to strengthen and provide a sense of security for Victims;
b. providing information regarding the rights of Victims to obtain Protection from the police and the determination of Protection orders from the court;
c. escorting Victims to Safe Houses or alternative residences; and
d. conducting integrated coordination in providing services to Victims with agencies or related parties needed by Victims.

heading: Article 28
heading_path: HANDLING OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 28

1. The Regional Government shall prepare Safe Houses.
2. Safe Houses as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be used for temporary handling of Victims of Violence against Women and Children.
3. Safe Houses as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be provided in every Sub-district.

heading: Article 29
heading_path: HANDLING OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 29

1. Advocates as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (1) letter c shall assist in providing legal services for Victims or provide legal consultation in the form of information regarding the rights of Victims and the judicial process;
2. Advocates shall accompany and/or represent Victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings.
3. Information on violence from Victims that is personal in nature shall be kept confidential by advocates.
4. Advocates may coordinate with fellow law enforcers, companion volunteers, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

heading: Article 30
heading_path: HANDLING OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 30

Religious leaders as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (1) letter d shall have the duty to:
a. provide spiritual guidance or strengthening of faith and piety to Victims; and
b. provide explanations regarding the rights and obligations of Victims.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Part One

Guidance

heading: Article 31
translated_text:
Article 31

1. The Regional Government shall carry out guidance for Women and Children.
2. Guidance for Women and Children as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted through:
a. socialization;
b. guidance; and/or
c. training.
3. Guidance for Women and Children shall be carried out by Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of empowerment of Women and Children.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Supervision

heading: Article 32
translated_text:
Article 32

1. The Regional Government shall conduct supervision in the context of Protection of Women and Children.
2. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted by means of monitoring and evaluation.
3. Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out periodically at least 2 (two) times a year.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 33

1. The community shall participate in efforts to protect Women and Children.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in the form of:
a. providing data or information regarding Women and Children who have not received fulfillment of rights from the Regional Government;
b. providing information on every condition that tends to lead to acts of violence against Women and Children to the authorized party and/or Regional Government; and/or
c. promoting the Protection of Women and Children.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

FUNDING

Article 34

1. Funding for the implementation of Protection of Women and Children shall be charged to:
a. the state revenue and expenditure budget;
b. the regional revenue and expenditure budget; and
c. other lawful and non-binding sources.
2. Funding as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a shall be budgeted in the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of empowerment of Women and Children.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 35

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by its placement in the Regional Gazette of Pasangkayu Regency.

Enacted in Pasangkayu on 18 November 2019

heading: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF PASANGKAYU REGENCY
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF PASANGKAYU REGENCY

NUMBER 9 YEAR 2019 CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF PASANGKAYU REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

Protection from violence that threatens the safety of Women and Children must be provided from an early stage. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. For example, Women and Children become Victims of persecution, neglect, eviction and ill-treatment by parents or other persons. For Women and Children experiencing such problems, the Regional Government must provide Safe Houses and adequate budget.

Likewise, the role of various parties to help address the violence issues faced by Women and Children must be in synergy with the programs and activities of the Regional Government. Social community organizations, volunteers, social workers, medical personnel, advocates and religious leaders must also be mobilized and can participate in providing and enhancing a sense of security for Women and Children.

For the Regional Government of Pasangkayu Regency, a concrete step to create a legal umbrella in order to provide and enhance a sense of security and prevent acts of violence against Women and Children, is by establishing a Regional Regulation on Protection for Children and Women. Furthermore, the implementation of protection of Women and Children shall be carried out based on the principles of: justice; respect for the rights of Victims; justice and gender equality; non-discrimination; and the best interests of Victims.
